ISTJ>INTJ.title: Before deciding, you look back at how it was done last year.
ISTJ>INTJ.body: When you decide something, you check what came before, then think all the way ahead. Even when you buy furniture, you think about whether it'll still work after you move. When you plan how work will go, you look back at last year's way and think about next year too. People often tell you you're good at making plans.
ISTJ>INTJ.body_s: When you decide something, you check what came before, then think all the way ahead. Even when you buy a bag, you think about whether you'll still use it next year. When you plan your club's practice menu, you look back at last year's way and think about next year too. People often tell you you're good at making plans.
ISTJ>INTJ.say: "I want to think about three years from now, too."
ISTJ>INTJ.do: When you buy a phone, you pick one based on how many years it'll last.
ISTJ>INTJ.worry: You can't easily decide whether to stick with the old way or try a new one. Some days you have so much on your mind that your head never gets a break.
ISTJ>INTJ.karai: You turned down an invite because you "had plans." The plan was cleaning your room.
ISTJ>INTJ.aru: You start planning a trip and end up looking up towns you'd like to live in. Suddenly it's midnight, and you still haven't booked a place to stay.
ISTJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks based on past experience and things that are certain. As the years went by, you also started picturing things many years ahead. Taking your time to look things up and decide on your own hasn't changed since way back. To pick a place to stay, you first want to know about the town, and once you look up the town, you start imagining what living there would be like, so before you know it you've drifted away from planning the trip.
ISTJ>INTJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. If you answer while thinking about work, you lean toward facts. If you think about the future, you lean toward ideas.
ISTJ>INTJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. If you answer while thinking about your daily classes and homework, you lean toward facts. If you think about the future, you lean toward ideas.
ISTJ>INTJ.plus: It takes you a while to decide because you think things through carefully. Plenty of people probably feel safe with a plan you made.
ISTJ>INTJ.tip: Try setting a 30-minute timer before you start looking things up. When it rings, you can ask yourself, "What was I supposed to decide today?"
ISTJ>INTJ.hidden: Do you quickly notice when someone's story doesn't match what they said before? That comes from your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Before deciding on something new, look at last year's results. People will find it easier to say yes.

ISTJ>INTP.title: Someone who wonders, "Why is it done this way?"
ISTJ>INTP.body: You follow set steps properly. But while you're doing them, you start to wonder, "Why do we do it this way in the first place?" Even when watching the news, you want to know where the numbers came from and go looking for the original source. While looking into it, you sometimes find a better way.
ISTJ>INTP.say: "This order works, but why is it in this order?"
ISTJ>INTP.do: When buying an appliance, you compare the specs yourself before asking the staff.
ISTJ>INTP.do_s: When buying earbuds, you compare the specs yourself before asking the staff.
ISTJ>INTP.worry: You want to follow the rules, but you also want to try another way, so you get stuck. Thinking is fun for you, so sometimes you end up rushing right before a deadline.
ISTJ>INTP.karai: In a meeting where everyone's supposed to decide together, you've already reached the answer on your own.
ISTJ>INTP.karai_s: In a class discussion where everyone's supposed to decide together, you've already reached the answer on your own.
ISTJ>INTP.aru: You were reading the manual, and now you're watching a video about how the thing works. The day before a deadline, you somehow can't stop.
ISTJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type who follows written steps exactly as they are. Through all kinds of experiences, your interest turned toward how things work, "Why does it happen this way?", and you also started taking detours when something catches your attention. Getting quietly lost in thought on your own has been part of you all along. The more you need to focus on the steps, the more the "why" behind them stays on your mind, so even the day before a deadline, you can't stop looking into how things work.
ISTJ>INTP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. If you picture work with a deadline, your answers come out more structured. If you picture looking things up on a day off, they come out freer.
ISTJ>INTP.yure_s: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. If you picture an assignment with a deadline, your answers come out more structured. If you picture looking things up on a day off, they come out freer.
ISTJ>INTP.plus: You get stuck because you notice there might be a better way. You usually follow the rules, so when you say, "We should fix this part," people listen.
ISTJ>INTP.tip: When a video or article catches your eye, don't watch it right away. Just leave the tab open. If you look at it after you're done, you won't panic before deadlines.
ISTJ>INTP.hidden: Even if you think you go with the flow, do you lay out everything you'll pack the night before a trip? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it at work too, and you'll see your ideas through to the end.
ISTJ>INTP.hidden_s: Even if you think you go with the flow, do you lay out everything you'll pack the night before a trip? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it on your assignments too, and you'll see your ideas through to the end.

ISTJ>ENTJ.title: Someone who prepares well and pulls the discussion together.
ISTJ>ENTJ.body: Before a meeting you read the materials carefully, and at the end you're the one who wraps up with, "Okay, let's do it this way." Before a discussion, you narrow down what you want to decide to three things and write them on paper. You often lead conversations in front of people, but afterward you want time alone to rest.
ISTJ>ENTJ.body_s: Before a discussion you read the handouts carefully, and at the end you're the one who wraps up with, "Okay, let's do it this way." Before a discussion, you narrow down what you want to decide to three things and write them in your notebook. You often lead conversations in front of people, but afterward you want time alone to rest.
ISTJ>ENTJ.say: "I've checked the numbers. Let's raise it a little next year."
ISTJ>ENTJ.say_s: "I've checked last year's member count. Let's raise it a little next year."
ISTJ>ENTJ.do: You put all of next month's plans into your calendar early.
ISTJ>ENTJ.worry: Because you work hard in front of others, your alone time keeps getting pushed back. You often can't decide whether to play it safe or go for it.
ISTJ>ENTJ.karai: Even on your day off, you're planning next week in your head.
ISTJ>ENTJ.aru: At meetings you lead everyone, but at home you can't get off the couch. You decide your replies can wait until tomorrow.
ISTJ>ENTJ.aru_s: At club meetings you lead everyone, but at home you can't get off the couch. You decide your replies can wait until tomorrow.
ISTJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges with quiet time alone and relies on how things have been done before. As you gained experience, you also came to stand in front of people and show the direction ahead. Even after becoming able to lead people, where you recharge is the same as ever. You use up energy the whole time you're leading in front of people, so when you get home, your body and mind both shut down and you have no energy left even to type a reply.
ISTJ>ENTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your meeting-day self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ENTJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your club-meeting-day self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ENTJ.plus: Wanting a break doesn't mean you're weak. It means you work hard every day.
ISTJ>ENTJ.tip: On days with a big meeting, decide ahead of time not to make evening plans. Then it's easier to say "Not that day" when someone invites you.
ISTJ>ENTJ.tip_s: On days with a big discussion or presentation, decide ahead of time not to make evening plans. Then it's easier to say "Not that day" when someone invites you.
ISTJ>ENTJ.hidden: Even when deciding on something new, do you first ask, "How did last month go?" That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Because of it, people think, "If it's this person, it'll be fine."

ISTJ>ENTP.title: Someone who throws out ideas, then looks into them properly.
ISTJ>ENTP.body: It may look like you're just talking off the top of your head, but afterward you actually look into it. When you hear someone's idea, you build on it right there: "Wouldn't it be more fun if we did it this way?" Some days you want to talk and be lively, and some days you want quiet time alone. Sometimes you surprise a friend by saying, "I looked into what we talked about the other day."
ISTJ>ENTP.say: "Didn't we try that before, and it didn't work?"
ISTJ>ENTP.do: When the family can't pick a trip, you line up the cost of each place and compare.
ISTJ>ENTP.worry: You come up with so many ideas that you wear yourself out trying to pick one. The gap between days you want to talk and days you don't want to see anyone is big, and it confuses even you.
ISTJ>ENTP.karai: You toss out all kinds of opposite ideas, then pick the safest option in the end.
ISTJ>ENTP.aru: At a party you say, "Wouldn't it be fun to do this?" That night on the train home, you're looking up costs and dates.
ISTJ>ENTP.aru_s: While eating out with friends, you say, "Wouldn't it be fun to do this?" That night on the train home, you're looking up costs and dates.
ISTJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type who checks things on your own first and then moves forward as decided. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started coming up with new ideas while talking with people. The ideas come when you're talking with people, and the checking happens once you're alone. You're uneasy leaving something you said as just a passing idea, so once you're alone, you want to check with real numbers whether it can actually be done.
ISTJ>ENTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result changes easily. Answer as your idea-sharing self and you'll get a lively, free result. Answer as your quietly-researching self and you'll get a calm, structured one.
ISTJ>ENTP.plus: You can't narrow down your ideas because you have so many. And since you check on what you said later, people tend to trust you.
ISTJ>ENTP.tip: Decide, "If I still want to do it a week later, I'll do it." After a busy, social day, keep the next day free of plans so the tiredness doesn't stick around.
ISTJ>ENTP.hidden: When talking one-on-one, can you listen quietly until the other person is done? That's your temperament, which likes to think things through alone. Value it, and friends will start saying you're easy to talk to.

ISTJ>INFJ.title: Someone who thinks it through with you when you need advice.
ISTJ>INFJ.body: When someone comes to you with a problem, you first sort out what happened in order, then think together with them about what they want to do. You like to have weekend plans settled by Wednesday, and before deciding, you take time to think alone. You say what needs to be said, but before you do, you swap words around in your head again and again so the other person won't get hurt.
ISTJ>INFJ.say: "Okay, I get the situation. So what do you want to do?"
ISTJ>INFJ.do: You set the date and the restaurant for plans with friends a month ahead.
ISTJ>INFJ.worry: When the right thing and the kind thing are different, you can't decide which to say. You do so much for others that your own feelings get put off.
ISTJ>INFJ.karai: Somehow you're always the one sorting out dates in the group chat.
ISTJ>INFJ.aru: While listening to a friend's love problems, you're planning in your head: "First say this, then..." You go back and forth on whether to say it or keep quiet, and can't fall asleep that night.
ISTJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who sorts facts in order and thinks with logic. As you gained experience, you also started picturing the other person's feelings and how things will go from here. These days, your ability to sort things out and your care for the other person work at the same time. You think saying it might help them, but you also think it might hurt them, so you keep thinking into the night without being able to decide which is better.
ISTJ>INFJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>INFJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture homework or a class job and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>INFJ.plus: Hesitating shows you really think about how the other person feels. You can say hard things in a way that gets through.
ISTJ>INFJ.tip: When someone asks for advice, first ask, "Do you want me to listen, or think it through with you?" Once you know what they want, you'll spend less time unsure.
ISTJ>INFJ.hidden: When a friend talks about a dream, do you want to ask, "When will you start? What do you need?" That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. With it, plans that might stay just talk actually get moving.

ISTJ>INFP.title: Someone who finishes the to-dos, then gets lost in what they love.
ISTJ>INFP.body: You finish what needs doing properly by the deadline. After that, you lose track of time in the things you love. On weekends, you clear everything off your desk first, then start reading a favorite novel. Watching one favorite movie after work might be something you look forward to.
ISTJ>INFP.body_s: You finish what needs doing properly by the deadline. After that, you lose track of time in the things you love. On the day tests end, you tidy up your desk first, then start reading a favorite manga. Watching one favorite movie after finishing an assignment might be something you look forward to.
ISTJ>INFP.say: "I've finished what you asked. I'll head home now."
ISTJ>INFP.do: On days off, you walk around your neighborhood alone, listening to your favorite songs.
ISTJ>INFP.worry: Some days "I should do this properly" and "I want to do what I like" pop up at the same time, and you end up stuck in between. When you understand something in your head but your heart doesn't follow, you blame yourself.
ISTJ>INFP.karai: The day after a fun party, you don't reply to anyone and just lie around at home.
ISTJ>INFP.karai_s: The day after a fun team party, you don't reply to anyone and just lie around at home.
ISTJ>INFP.aru: Every morning you get up at the same time and do chores in the same order. On a day off you think, "I'd like to see the ocean," and next thing you know you're looking up train transfers in detail.
ISTJ>INFP.aru_s: Every morning you get up at the same time and get ready for school in the same order. On a day off you think, "I'd like to see the ocean," and next thing you know you're looking up train transfers in detail.
ISTJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type who goes through each day properly, with set routines. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value feelings that suddenly come to you, and you started to enjoy heading out on a whim too. You have both a side that gets sudden ideas and a side that prepares properly. The wish to see the ocean may come out of nowhere, but getting lost on an unfamiliar route makes you uneasy, so before you leave you want to check even the train transfers.
ISTJ>INFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your weekday self or as your self doing what you love can give totally different results.
ISTJ>INFP.plus: Days when your heart doesn't follow show that you really feel your own feelings. Having time for what you love keeps you going on weekdays.
ISTJ>INFP.tip: Once a week, decide "this time is just for what I like" and put it in your calendar. If it's a plan, you won't feel like you're slacking while you enjoy it.
ISTJ>INFP.hidden: While listening to a friend's problem, are you thinking somewhere in your head, "The cause is probably this"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Listen kindly first, then use it, and people will count on you to help find answers.

ISTJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who doesn't just cheer you on, but helps you prepare.
ISTJ>ENFJ.body: When you cheer someone on, you don't stop at words; you help them prepare too. When you hear a friend is starting something new, you might make a list of what they'll need and hand it to them. You take on the role of speaking at the morning meeting, but at lunch you want to go outside alone and eat your packed lunch.
ISTJ>ENFJ.say: "You'll do great on tomorrow's test. I'm rooting for you."
ISTJ>ENFJ.do: For a friend's birthday party, you decide early who handles the gift and the cake.
ISTJ>ENFJ.worry: The harder you try to meet everyone's expectations, the less alone time you get. You often can't decide whether to put feelings first or stick to the rules.
ISTJ>ENFJ.karai: You praise other people a lot, but about yourself you only say, "I'm not there yet."
ISTJ>ENFJ.aru: You help a junior practice a presentation and clap, "That was great!" On the way home, you message them, "They might ask about this part."
ISTJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who prepares on your own and thinks with facts and logic. As the years went by, you also came to encourage people and stay close to how they feel. The encouraging words are something you picked up through experience, and preparing ahead has always been your strong point. You think clapping alone might leave them stuck on the real day, so you want to tell them ahead of time what they're likely to be asked.
ISTJ>ENFJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as yourself cheering someone on or as yourself preparing alone can flip the result.
ISTJ>ENFJ.plus: You overdo it because seeing people try hard makes you truly happy. When a senior helps even with the prep, younger people feel at ease.
ISTJ>ENFJ.tip: On days you help someone, tell them at the start when you'll finish. Saying "That's it for today" won't put them in a bind.
ISTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do good ideas come to you while reading or walking alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Put that time in your schedule, and your energy for supporting others will last longer.

ISTJ>ENFP.title: Someone who starts on a whim and keeps it up for a long time.
ISTJ>ENFP.body: You start new things on impulse, yet before you know it you've kept them up for a long time. For things you've started, you make a small mark on your calendar and count how many days in a row you've kept going. You might be the only one still going to the lessons a friend talked you into starting.
ISTJ>ENFP.say: "This looks fun. Let's try it once!"
ISTJ>ENFP.do: When you find an event that looks interesting, you message a friend right away: "Want to go?"
ISTJ>ENFP.worry: New things excite you, but when changes keep coming, you suddenly get tired. Some days, after acting on impulse, you scold yourself, "I need to get it together."
ISTJ>ENFP.karai: You say "I'm in!" right away, but you already picked out your outfit the night before.
ISTJ>ENFP.aru: You say you started your balcony garden "just for fun." But you water it every morning without fail, and on trip days you ask your family to take over before you leave.
ISTJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type who keeps up what you decided on your own, properly, every day. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started trying new things on the momentum of a conversation. All four letters are different: how you start things is something you picked up through experience, and how you keep them going is something you were born with. Even if the reason you started was casual, repeating the same thing at the same time every day doesn't bother you, so the watering just keeps going naturally.
ISTJ>ENFP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your day-out-with-friends self or your usual weekday self could give opposite results.
ISTJ>ENFP.plus: You look back after acting on impulse because you want to take care of what you started. Not many people can keep up the things they started on a whim.
ISTJ>ENFP.tip: When you start something new, try deciding "just two weeks to begin with." It's easy to jump in, and you can calmly decide whether to keep going.
ISTJ>ENFP.hidden: You seem to go with the flow, but when shopping, do you carefully compare prices and reviews? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it at work, and your ideas will sound convincing and get people moving.
ISTJ>ENFP.hidden_s: You seem to go with the flow, but when shopping, do you carefully compare prices and reviews? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it in clubs or group projects, and your ideas will sound convincing and get people moving.

ISTJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who keeps their promises.
ISTJ>ISTJ.body: Whatever you're asked to do is done by the day before the deadline. You log receipts in your household budget the same day, so your numbers almost never fail to add up at the end of the month. You do your best work where the steps are clear, but in places where everything gets decided on a whim, you tend to tire out quickly.
ISTJ>ISTJ.body_s: Whatever you're asked to do is done by the day before the deadline. You organize your notes during that day's classes, so you rarely panic before tests. You do your best in classes and clubs where the steps are clear, but in places where everything gets decided on a whim, you tend to tire out quickly.
ISTJ>ISTJ.say: "Let me check how it went last time, then I'll get back to you."
ISTJ>ISTJ.say_s: "Let me check how it went last time, then I'll let you know."
ISTJ>ISTJ.do: You always arrive ten minutes early to meet someone.
ISTJ>ISTJ.worry: Sudden changes of plans and unclear instructions wear you out. You wonder if something's wrong with you, but often the way things are done just doesn't suit you.
ISTJ>ISTJ.karai: When told "Just do it however," you ask, "How much is 'however'?"
ISTJ>ISTJ.aru: Before a trip, you can't relax until you've looked up even the transfer times. When someone says, "Let's decide as we go today," you get a little restless.
ISTJ>ISTJ.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination, so your way of checking before you act has carried on just as it is since way back. Having quiet time alone to prepare puts you at ease. When plans are clear, you can relax and enjoy the day itself. If you head out with things still unknown, you keep worrying about whether you'll get lost on a transfer, so you want to look things up first and clear away the worry.
ISTJ>ISTJ.yure: Your temperament and character match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day when sudden changes have worn you out, your answers may come out a little different.
ISTJ>ISTJ.plus: Unclear things tire you out because you want to finish things properly. Thanks to your checking, the people around you make far fewer mistakes.
ISTJ>ISTJ.tip: When a conversation is vague, try asking, "So, by what time should we decide?" That alone makes a big difference in how tired you get.
ISTJ>ISTJ.hidden: On a trip, have you ever wandered into a small shop that wasn't on the plan and had a great time? Going with the moment is something you can do, too. Leave some free time now and then, and time with friends will get even more fun.

ISTJ>ISFJ.title: Someone people feel safe having around.
ISTJ>ISFJ.body: At work and at home, people often tell you, "It's reassuring when you're here." You come in at the same time every morning and give the shared desk a quick wipe. Your work has few mistakes, and when someone seems busy, you might quietly pick up the phone for them.
ISTJ>ISFJ.body_s: At school and at home, people often tell you, "It's reassuring when you're here." You get to class early in the morning and quietly erase what was left on the board. Your assignments and class jobs have few mistakes, and when someone seems busy, you might quietly help hand out the worksheets.
ISTJ>ISFJ.say: "I've already printed the handouts for tomorrow's meeting."
ISTJ>ISFJ.say_s: "I already printed the slides for tomorrow's presentation."
ISTJ>ISFJ.do: When supplies at work run low, you order more before anyone asks.
ISTJ>ISFJ.do_s: When the athletic tape in the club room runs low, you buy more before anyone asks.
ISTJ>ISFJ.worry: Even when something needs to be said, you worry it'll hurt the other person and sometimes can't say it. As you keep saying yes to favors, your own time disappears.
ISTJ>ISFJ.karai: When someone asks, "Want some help?", you end up saying, "I'm fine."
ISTJ>ISFJ.aru: You spot a mistake in a coworker's paperwork, but worry they'll feel bad if you say something, so you quietly fix it. Before you know it, you're taking other people's work home.
ISTJ>ISFJ.aru_s: You spot a mistake in a groupmate's report, but worry they'll feel bad if you say something, so you quietly fix it. Before you know it, you're taking other people's parts home.
ISTJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who uses logic to point out mistakes clearly. As you gained experience, you also started thinking first about how the person hearing it will feel. Your eye for spotting mistakes is the same as ever; what's changed is how you bring it up. You feel that quietly fixing it yourself is faster and hurts no one, compared to pointing it out and getting them down, so you end up taking it on.
ISTJ>ISFJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>ISFJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture homework or class jobs and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>ISFJ.plus: You can't say it because you understand how the other person feels. Someone accurate and kind is a person everyone at work can count on.
ISTJ>ISFJ.plus_s: You can't say it because you understand how the other person feels. Someone accurate and kind is a person everyone in class or in the club can count on.
ISTJ>ISFJ.tip: When you notice a mistake, don't fix it quietly. Just say, "The date here was wrong." They'll be careful next time, and you won't end up with extra work.
ISTJ>ISFJ.tip_s: When you notice a mistake, don't fix it quietly. Just say, "This number was off." They'll be careful next time, and you won't end up with extra work.
ISTJ>ISFJ.hidden: When picking an appliance or a place to move, do you compare prices and convenience one by one before deciding? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Try using it when you can't decide because you're thinking too much about others' feelings.
ISTJ>ISFJ.hidden_s: When picking a phone or a bike for getting to school, do you compare prices and convenience one by one before deciding? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Try using it when you can't decide because you're thinking too much about others' feelings.

ISTJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who prepares alone, then runs the show on the day.
ISTJ>ESTJ.body: People tend to think, "If we leave it to them, it'll be fine." You look back over your notes from the last get-together and buy whatever ran short ahead of time. You do the preparation quietly on your own, and on the day you stand in front of everyone and call out to them.
ISTJ>ESTJ.say: "Three things to do today. Let's go in this order."
ISTJ>ESTJ.do: At the supermarket, you go through the aisles in the order of what you need to buy.
ISTJ>ESTJ.do_s: When shopping for the school festival, you go through the aisles in the order of what you need to buy.
ISTJ>ESTJ.worry: The more people rely on you, the more often you're in front of others, and your alone time shrinks. On days you're too harsh with someone who's careless, you quietly regret it later.
ISTJ>ESTJ.karai: You tell others "Rest is part of the job," but you haven't used a single day of your own paid leave.
ISTJ>ESTJ.karai_s: You tell others "Rest matters too," but you haven't skipped a single day of club practice.
ISTJ>ESTJ.aru: You handle the work party well as the organizer, but once it's over you want to be alone right away, so you skip the after-party saying, "I have an early morning."
ISTJ>ESTJ.aru_s: You handle the team party well as the organizer, but once it's over you want to be alone right away, so you skip the karaoke afterward saying, "I have an early morning."
ISTJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by quiet time alone. Through all kinds of experiences, you also became able to stand in front of people and get everyone moving. How solidly you prepare hasn't changed since way back. While you're organizing, you spend your energy on doing your part, so once it's over, you want quiet time alone more than the next get-together.
ISTJ>ESTJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-at-work self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ESTJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-your-club-or-class self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ESTJ.plus: You can look back and regret it because you really pay attention to people. Leaders like that are trusted for a long time.
ISTJ>ESTJ.tip: When you schedule an event, keep the next morning free too. It also helps to decide, "I'll go to the after-party for just the first 30 minutes."
ISTJ>ESTJ.hidden: On nights after you've run things, do you look back alone and think, "How did today go?" That comes from your temperament, which likes to think things through alone. Use it, and you'll run the next get-together even better.

ISTJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who carefully gets a get-together ready.
ISTJ>ESFJ.body: When there's a get-together, you pin down the date, the restaurant, and the seating, and you even remember what everyone likes. When setting the date, you ask about everyone's schedule and put it in a chart before deciding. The day after a lively gathering, you want to be quiet on your own. At family gatherings with relatives, before you know it you're going back and forth between the kitchen and the table.
ISTJ>ESFJ.say: "Everyone can make it on this day, so let's go with it."
ISTJ>ESFJ.do: When someone at work is off, you take their calls too.
ISTJ>ESFJ.do_s: When someone with a class job is absent, you hand out the papers for them too.
ISTJ>ESFJ.worry: While looking after everyone, your alone time vanishes and you suddenly feel drained. You want people to follow the rules, but you don't want to blame them either, and you get stuck.
ISTJ>ESFJ.karai: When you organize, your own seat is always by the door.
ISTJ>ESFJ.aru: As organizer of a farewell party, you even ask what foods everyone dislikes. But when someone asks, "What do you want to eat?" you can't answer right away.
ISTJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks on your own and decides with logic. As you gained experience, you also came to move among people and go along with how everyone feels. You've gotten good at gathering what other people like, but you're still not very used to saying what you like yourself. You spend the whole time preparing thinking about everyone's wishes, so when someone suddenly asks about you, an answer doesn't come right away.
ISTJ>ESFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your party-organizer self or your quiet-day-alone self.
ISTJ>ESFJ.plus: You get stuck because you care about both the rules and people's feelings. When you're there, get-togethers run smoothly.
ISTJ>ESFJ.tip: When you're the organizer, add one dish you want to eat. You'll feel, "I'm allowed to enjoy this too," and you'll be less tired afterward.
ISTJ>ESFJ.hidden: When it's time to split the bill or decide who does what, can you decide without hesitating? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and people will think, "If they're in charge, it'll be fair."

ISTJ>ISTP.title: Someone who fixes things as soon as they break.
ISTJ>ISTP.body: Even when something goes wrong, you don't panic and quickly fix it with whatever's on hand. You remember where all the tools and batteries in the house are, and when something breaks, you take a look yourself first. Some days you prepare ahead, and some days you figure it out on the spot. Even if your bike chain comes off, you crouch down and fix it right there.
ISTJ>ISTP.say: "I fixed it for now. I'll make sure it doesn't happen again."
ISTJ>ISTP.do: When a light bulb burns out, you replace it right away and buy a spare while you're at it.
ISTJ>ISTP.worry: Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood, so it's hard to find your own pace. You don't like being tied down by rules, but you can't relax when nothing is decided.
ISTJ>ISTP.karai: You say, "I don't read manuals," but you read the troubleshooting page carefully.
ISTJ>ISTP.aru: You say, "It'll work out," yet you always charge your phone to full before you head out.
ISTJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who feels at ease when you've prepared ahead of time. As the years went by, you gained confidence that you can handle whatever comes up on the spot. Even though you can handle things on the spot now, your habit of preparing is still there as it always was. You know you can only handle things on the spot because you've done the bare minimum to prepare, so you always charge your phone to full before you head out.
ISTJ>ISTP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a work deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISTJ>ISTP.yure_s: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a homework deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISTJ>ISTP.plus: It's hard to find your pace because you can switch depending on the moment. Someone who fixes things on the spot and prepares for next time is a big help.
ISTJ>ISTP.tip: On days off, try planning only half the day, like "plans in the morning, nothing in the afternoon." You won't feel restless, and you can still relax.
ISTJ>ISTP.hidden: Before an exam or a move, do you naturally decide what to take care of first? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it for big goals, and you'll finish even the things you started on a whim.

ISTJ>ISFP.title: Someone who adds a bit of their own taste to the usual way.
ISTJ>ISFP.body: You do what's set properly, but you add a little of your own taste to it. Even on the same route you walk every day, you slow down a little at the corner where seasonal flowers are blooming. When choosing clothes, you stick to your usual styles but change the color depending on your mood that day.
ISTJ>ISFP.say: "It's cold today, so I'll put some ginger in the soup."
ISTJ>ISFP.say_s: "It's cold today, so I put some ginger in the hot cocoa."
ISTJ>ISFP.do: You measure everything to follow the recipe, then taste it and change it just a little at the end.
ISTJ>ISFP.do_s: When baking, you measure everything to follow the recipe, then taste it and change it just a little at the end.
ISTJ>ISFP.worry: You want to get the usual chores done, but some days you just feel like resting, and you can't decide. You're not good at putting your feelings into words, and it's frustrating when they don't come across.
ISTJ>ISFP.worry_s: You want to get your usual homework done, but some days you just feel like resting, and you can't decide. You're not good at putting your feelings into words, and it's frustrating when they don't come across.
ISTJ>ISFP.karai: Your day off was supposed to be relaxing, but it's filled with laundry and grocery runs.
ISTJ>ISFP.karai_s: Your day off was supposed to be relaxing, but it's filled with homework and cleaning your room.
ISTJ>ISFP.aru: You clean on the same days every week. You don't feel done until you open the window and put on your favorite music.
ISTJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who does what's set properly and logically. As you gained experience, you also came to value your mood that day and what feels good. These days, set routines and your own taste fit together in one way of doing things. You get through the cleaning with your set routine, then add a bit of time that feels good at the end, and only then does it feel finished.
ISTJ>ISFP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer thinking about work or chores and the result comes out structured. Answer thinking about your days off and it comes out softer.
ISTJ>ISFP.yure_s: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer thinking about classes or homework and the result comes out structured. Answer thinking about your days off and it comes out softer.
ISTJ>ISFP.plus: You struggle to put feelings into words because what you feel is detailed. Even when you don't say it, what you do for people often gets the message across.
ISTJ>ISFP.tip: When you can't say how you feel, it's okay to say, "Let me think about it." If you give one reason a little later, even a few words will get through.
ISTJ>ISFP.hidden: When picking a place to eat with friends, do you decide quickly by distance or price? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. When sharing your feelings, giving one reason makes them easier to understand.

ISTJ>ESTP.title: Someone who moves fast, but is already prepared.
ISTJ>ESTP.body: When something happens, you're the first to move. But behind that, you've been looking things up and preparing all along. You remember the exits at stations you use often and where the stores are, so you don't get lost when it counts. Even if plans change on a trip, you can decide the next place to go right away.
ISTJ>ESTP.say: "I looked up a route that works even in the rain. Let's go."
ISTJ>ESTP.do: If your bike tires are low, you pump them up before heading out.
ISTJ>ESTP.worry: The urge to move fast clashes with the urge to prepare so nothing goes wrong, and you get tired before deciding. After a lively day, you can easily feel off if you don't get quiet time alone.
ISTJ>ESTP.karai: The person who said "Let's just try it" read the reviews carefully before starting.
ISTJ>ESTP.aru: A friend says, "Let's go out now!" and you answer, "I'm in!" right away. But before you leave, you've looked up the train times for the way home.
ISTJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who prepares on your own and moves forward as decided. As you gained experience, you also came to move right away when people invite you and enjoy the moment. Even with the ease of jumping on invitations, your long-standing caution hasn't gone away. As long as you know how to get home, you can relax and have fun, so even after saying "I'm in!", you make sure to check the train times for the way home.
ISTJ>ESTP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your out-with-friends self or your preparing-alone self.
ISTJ>ESTP.plus: You over-prepare because you want everyone to relax and have fun. There's surely someone your preparing has helped.
ISTJ>ESTP.tip: After plans with friends, keep the next morning as alone time. Narrow what you bring to three "must-haves," and you can head out light.
ISTJ>ESTP.hidden: When you focus alone on cooking or building models, do you lose track of time? That's your temperament, which is good at quiet focus on your own. Use that focus at work, and people will see you as someone who gets it done.
ISTJ>ESTP.hidden_s: When you focus alone on cooking or building models, do you lose track of time? That's your temperament, which is good at quiet focus on your own. Use that focus for studying or your team, and people will see you as someone who gets it done.

ISTJ>ESFP.title: Someone who laughs a lot and still keeps an eye on the last train.
ISTJ>ESFP.title_s: Someone who laughs a lot and still keeps an eye on the time to head home.
ISTJ>ESFP.body: You brighten the mood, but you also keep an eye on when to head home and how much money is being spent. That's why the people with you can relax and have fun. When choosing a place, you trust what you thought when you went yourself more than online reviews. The day after a fun day, you want to take it easy on your own.
ISTJ>ESFP.say: "This place is so good! Let's come back again."
ISTJ>ESFP.do: When you find something tasty on a trip, you buy some for everyone.
ISTJ>ESFP.worry: The more fun you have, the more you want alone time afterward, and that surprises even you. You want to enjoy yourself fully, but you can't help thinking about what's next or about money.
ISTJ>ESFP.karai: You said, "Let's not plan anything today," but you've already booked the restaurant.
ISTJ>ESFP.aru: At karaoke, you're the most excited one. But ten minutes before the end, you've already figured out how much each person owes.
ISTJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who stays calm on your own and manages money and time logically. Through all kinds of experiences, you also became able to get excited along with everyone, just as you feel. Even when you're having a great time, the math in the back of your mind doesn't stop. Fumbling with the bill at the end bothers you, so even while singing, you want to have each person's share figured out before it's over.
ISTJ>ESFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your out-with-friends self or your home-alone self can give completely different results.
ISTJ>ESFP.plus: You think ahead while having fun because you want everyone to feel good until the end. It's a relief to have someone who livens things up and wraps them up too.
ISTJ>ESFP.tip: The day after fun plans, pick a time when you won't check the group chat. If you're not chasing replies, you can really rest with time alone.
ISTJ>ESFP.hidden: When friends are about to argue, do you suggest, "Okay, let's take turns like this"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and people will count on you when things get tough.

ISFJ>INTJ.title: Someone who thinks far ahead for the people they care about.
ISFJ>INTJ.body: You think far ahead and prepare for your family and friends. You write your family's plans on the calendar and spot days that might clash ahead of time. In discussions, you say what you want to say calmly and slowly. When planning a trip, you set the order so no one gets worn out.
ISFJ>INTJ.say: "Won't that plan get tough in six months?"
ISFJ>INTJ.do: You save a little at a time, years ahead, for a trip or a new car.
ISFJ>INTJ.do_s: You save a little at a time, months ahead, for a trip or a camera you want.
ISFJ>INTJ.worry: Even when you know it's better to be direct, picturing the other person's face makes your words stop. Some days you think so much about the future that you can't enjoy the present.
ISFJ>INTJ.karai: You say, "Either is fine," but you keep talking about the place you want to go.
ISFJ>INTJ.aru: On family outings, you check when the roads get busy and say, "Let's leave 30 minutes early."
ISFJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who values past experience and your family's feelings. As the years went by, you also came to think logically about how things will go from here. Caring about your family has been part of you all along, and now the ability to read ahead has been added. You can already picture your family getting tired and cranky on a crowded road, so to avoid that, you want to leave a little early.
ISFJ>INTJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work plans and you lean toward logic and ideas. Picture your family and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ISFJ>INTJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture your plans after graduation and you lean toward logic and ideas. Picture your family and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ISFJ>INTJ.plus: Your words stop because you don't want to hurt anyone. People trust someone who takes the time to say hard things kindly.
ISFJ>INTJ.tip: Try starting hard conversations with, "Can I say just one thing?" With a little lead-in, the other person can listen calmly.
ISFJ>INTJ.hidden: Do you remember your friends' favorite foods and things they told you before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can remember "they liked this" and work it into your plans.

ISFJ>INTP.title: Someone who helps people out and ends up knowing how things work.
ISFJ>INTP.body: While helping someone who asked, you end up becoming an expert on the subject. When something catches your interest, you read article after article that seems related, alone at night. When a friend asks, "How do you do this?", you get really into explaining it.
ISFJ>INTP.say: "I looked it up, and the way it works is really interesting."
ISFJ>INTP.do: When you find an appliance you want, you read other people's reviews late into the night before buying.
ISFJ>INTP.do_s: When you find a tablet you want, you read other people's reviews late into the night before buying.
ISFJ>INTP.worry: You get so absorbed in looking things up that you forget other things you had to do. You want to go along with people, but you also want to think alone, and some days that wears you out.
ISFJ>INTP.karai: When you have plans to meet people on a day off, you feel a little heavy the day before.
ISFJ>INTP.aru: You offer to fix a friend's computer, and while looking for the cause, it turns midnight. The other thing they asked you to do has completely slipped your mind.
ISFJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type who takes care of what people ask of you, one thing at a time. Through all kinds of experiences, you also came to dig into "Why does it happen this way?" with logic and head toward whatever catches your interest. What gets you to help is your long-standing love of looking after people, and from there, curiosity pulls you along. Stopping when you're right on the edge of finding the cause feels wrong to you, so you keep looking into it to the point of forgetting other things you had to do.
ISFJ>INTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your helping-someone self or your researching-alone self can give totally different results.
ISFJ>INTP.plus: You get absorbed because you really want to know. Someone who helps others with what they've learned is someone people rely on.
ISFJ>INTP.tip: Before you start looking something up, finish one other task first. After that, you can dig in as long as you like.
ISFJ>INTP.hidden: On days with something important, do you get ready ahead of time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can share what you've learned by the day you promised.

ISFJ>ENTJ.title: When it's time to decide, you decide clearly.
ISFJ>ENTJ.body: When a decision needs to be made, you make it clearly. But afterward, you make sure to check in with anyone who seems tired. Before deciding, you listen at least once to the views of people likely to disagree. When the work is done, you might hand out snacks to everyone with a "Thanks for all your hard work."
ISFJ>ENTJ.body_s: When a decision needs to be made, you make it clearly. But afterward, you make sure to check in with anyone who seems tired. Before deciding, you listen at least once to the views of people likely to disagree. When the school festival prep is done, you might hand out snacks to everyone with a "Thanks for all your hard work."
ISFJ>ENTJ.say: "Thanks for staying late yesterday. Thanks to you, we're on schedule."
ISFJ>ENTJ.say_s: "Thanks for staying after school yesterday. Thanks to you, we're on schedule."
ISFJ>ENTJ.do: At the start of the week, you decide what to do and in what order.
ISFJ>ENTJ.worry: When you keep leading people, you lose time to relax alone. Some nights, after being direct, you worry you said too much and can't sleep.
ISFJ>ENTJ.karai: You tell others "Don't overdo it," but your own schedule is packed through the weekend.
ISFJ>ENTJ.aru: In a meeting, you clearly say, "This is the direction we'll take." That night in the bath, you're wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ISFJ>ENTJ.aru_s: In a club meeting, you clearly say, "This is the way we'll do it." That night in the bath, you're wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ISFJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks on your own and decides with the feelings of the people around you in mind. As the years went by, you also came to stand in front of people, look ahead, and decide clearly with logic. Even now that you can speak plainly, you still care about the other person's feelings as much as ever. In the moment, you put what needs doing first and say it firmly, but once you're alone, you start to worry about how the people on the receiving end took it.
ISFJ>ENTJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your leading-at-work self or your relaxing-at-home self can change the result a lot.
ISFJ>ENTJ.yure_s: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your leading-your-club-or-class self or your relaxing-at-home self can change the result a lot.
ISFJ>ENTJ.plus: You worry enough to lose sleep because you don't want to hurt anyone. When someone decides when it's time to decide, everyone else can move without second-guessing.
ISFJ>ENTJ.tip: If you think you said too much, try saying just "Thanks for yesterday" the next day. That alone can make you feel a little lighter.
ISFJ>ENTJ.hidden: Can you tell someone's tired just by looking at their face? That comes from your temperament, which decides with feelings. Value it, and even when you have to be firm, your words are less likely to hurt.

ISFJ>ENTP.title: Someone who wonders, "Isn't there an easier way?"
ISFJ>ENTP.body: When you see the usual way of doing things, you think, "Couldn't this be easier?" When you get an idea in the middle of a conversation, "This might be faster," you can't help saying it out loud. You might even change the order of household chores so it's easier for everyone.
ISFJ>ENTP.body_s: When you see the usual way of doing things, you think, "Couldn't this be easier?" When you get an idea in the middle of a conversation, "This might be faster," you can't help saying it out loud. You might even change the order of cleaning duty so it's easier for everyone.
ISFJ>ENTP.say: "You do that by hand every time? It could be easier."
ISFJ>ENTP.do: When the group chat goes quiet, you send a slightly odd topic and get it going again.
ISFJ>ENTP.worry: After sharing an idea, you keep worrying, "Did I say too much?" When lively days keep coming, you suddenly want to be alone.
ISFJ>ENTP.karai: After telling a joke, you secretly check whether the other person laughed.
ISFJ>ENTP.aru: In a meeting you say, "What if we flip it around?" and surprise everyone. But the next day, you're also looking into what's good about the old way.
ISFJ>ENTP.aru_s: In a class discussion you say, "What if we flip it around?" and surprise everyone. But the next day, you're also looking into what's good about the old way.
ISFJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type who checks things on your own and sticks to the usual way of doing things. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started getting new ideas while talking with people and saying them right then and there. All four letters are different, so you have both the ability to come up with ideas and the ability to check things. After you speak up, you also start to worry about the feelings of people who've valued the old way, so by the next day you want to have looked into what's good about the old way too.
ISFJ>ENTP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your chatting-with-friends self or your quiet-at-home self could give opposite results.
ISFJ>ENTP.plus: You worry you said too much because you care about people. When the person with new ideas also thinks about others' feelings, everyone feels safe to speak up.
ISFJ>ENTP.tip: Before sharing an idea, try adding, "Can I say something a little odd?" The other person can get ready to listen, and you won't worry as much afterward.
ISFJ>ENTP.hidden: When someone's having a hard time, do you help without saying anything? That comes from your temperament, which decides with feelings. With it, you can come up with ideas while thinking about who they'll make things easier for.

ISFJ>INFJ.title: Someone who thinks about a friend's future with them.
ISFJ>INFJ.body: You listen closely to a friend and think together with them about what they want to do from here. You even remember a friend's favorite snacks and the topics they'd rather avoid, and you prepare a little before you meet. After helping someone with a problem, you never forget to ask, "How's it going since then?"
ISFJ>INFJ.say: "Let's take our time and think together about what you want to do next."
ISFJ>INFJ.do: After listening to a friend, you find a video they'd probably like and send it to them.
ISFJ>INFJ.worry: You feel other people's worries as if they were your own, and it wears you out. Some days you think so much about the future that you get anxious.
ISFJ>INFJ.karai: You want to set plans early, but on the morning of, you kind of want to stay home.
ISFJ>INFJ.aru: On days you hear a friend's worries, you keep thinking even at home, "I should have said this back then."
ISFJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who remembers well what happened and what people said. As the years went by, you also started picturing how things will go for the other person from here. Valuing people's feelings hasn't changed since way back. You remember that day's conversation in detail, and on top of that you think about how those words will shape what the other person does next, so other ways you could have said it come to mind again and again.
ISFJ>INFJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture daily chores or work and you lean toward facts. Picture the future and you lean toward ideas.
ISFJ>INFJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture your daily classes or club and you lean toward facts. Picture the future and you lean toward ideas.
ISFJ>INFJ.plus: Other people's worries tire you out because you understand how they feel. People feel relieved when someone like you listens.
ISFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you hear a friend's worries, listen to your favorite music before bed to reset. Asking "How's it going?" the next day is enough.
ISFJ>INFJ.hidden: Do you remember the ways that worked well before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can say, "You mentioned this before," which helps people feel at ease.

ISFJ>INFP.title: Someone who thinks about what suits a person and picks it for them.
ISFJ>INFP.body: You think about people and you're good at choosing things that suit them. When choosing a present, you visit store after store while remembering things the person mentioned before. Music and movies you love move you deeply, and you listen to or rewatch them again and again. Some days you want things to go as planned, and some days you want to decide by mood.
ISFJ>INFP.say: "This song makes me want to cry every time I hear it."
ISFJ>INFP.do: You decide on souvenirs ahead of time, but if you see something at the shop that suits someone, you buy one more.
ISFJ>INFP.worry: You prepared ahead, but right before, you want to change it: "Actually, this one's better." Your feelings move easily, and some days little things bring you down.
ISFJ>INFP.karai: Before sending a message to someone you like, you reread it about three times.
ISFJ>INFP.aru: You had a birthday present ready a month ahead, but the night before you get a sudden idea and start redoing the wrapping.
ISFJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type who prepares early and moves forward as decided. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started turning ideas that come to you into something real on the spot. Preparing early has always been you, and the last-minute ideas came out through experience. The closer the day you give it, the more clearly you can picture the person's happy face, so when you think of a way to make them even happier, you can't help redoing it.
ISFJ>INFP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture daily chores and you answer in a structured way. Picture doing what you love and you answer more freely.
ISFJ>INFP.yure_s: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture your daily homework and you answer in a structured way. Picture doing what you love and you answer more freely.
ISFJ>INFP.plus: You want to redo things at the last minute because you want the person to be even happier. Something chosen with that much thought stays with them.
ISFJ>INFP.tip: Decide that you won't touch the present the night before. Save any new ideas for next time.
ISFJ>INFP.hidden: Do you handle daily chores and work properly, in a set order? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can keep doing what you love little by little.
ISFJ>INFP.hidden_s: Do you handle your daily homework and getting ready properly, in a set order? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can keep doing what you love little by little.

ISFJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who reaches out to everyone and leads them along.
ISFJ>ENFJ.body: You call out to everyone and lead them in the same direction. You also notice how each person is doing. You set dates for get-togethers early, and afterward you let people who couldn't come know what happened. In your hobby group, you might tell someone who hasn't come in a while, "Come next time."
ISFJ>ENFJ.body_s: You call out to everyone and lead them in the same direction. You also notice how each person is doing. You tell everyone the club schedule early, and afterward you let anyone who missed it know what happened. In your club, you might tell someone who hasn't been coming to practice, "Come next time."
ISFJ>ENFJ.say: "You looked worn out yesterday. Are you okay now?"
ISFJ>ENFJ.do: When no one replies to someone's post in the group chat, you send a sticker right away.
ISFJ>ENFJ.worry: While looking after everyone, some days you don't notice you're tired. When you're in front of people day after day, you start wanting to be alone.
ISFJ>ENFJ.karai: You're quick to carry other people's bags, but you never let anyone carry yours.
ISFJ>ENFJ.aru: After saying in your hobby group, "Let's set a goal together!" you contact each person who couldn't come. Only after you're done do you notice you're exhausted.
ISFJ>ENFJ.aru_s: After saying at your club, "Let's set a goal together!" you contact each person who couldn't come. Only after you're done do you notice you're exhausted.
ISFJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and values the way things have been. As you gained experience, you also came to stand in front of people and lead everyone toward a goal ahead. Even now that you can speak in front of people, the way you recharge is the same as when you were born. If even one person is left behind, you feel the goal you set won't belong to everyone, so even when you're tired, you want to contact every single person.
ISFJ>ENFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as yourself with people at work or at a get-together, or as yourself alone at home.
ISFJ>ENFJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as yourself with people in your club or class, or as yourself alone at home.
ISFJ>ENFJ.plus: You don't notice your own tiredness because you're paying so much attention to others. With someone like you in charge, everyone feels safe following along.
ISFJ>ENFJ.tip: After you finish contacting everyone, put your phone down and rest for the next hour. You'll notice your own tiredness more easily.
ISFJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved reading a favorite book or tidying your room alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Value that time, and you can keep looking after everyone for longer.

ISFJ>ENFP.title: Someone who invites everyone and checks that no one's on their own.
ISFJ>ENFP.body: When you find something that looks fun, you invite everyone right away. Once you've invited people, you make sure no one who comes ends up alone. When inviting people, you think about the mix so no one ends up knowing nobody there. At a barbecue, you might casually sit next to someone who hasn't joined the conversation.
ISFJ>ENFP.say: "That sounds fun! I want to try it too."
ISFJ>ENFP.do: When you and a friend decide to start a new hobby, you set the next meet-up date right there.
ISFJ>ENFP.worry: After a lively time, you suddenly want to be alone and sometimes turn down invites. Sometimes after acting on a whim, you worry, "I should've prepared better."
ISFJ>ENFP.karai: You invited people "just because," but you're the one who prepared the most.
ISFJ>ENFP.aru: You love asking, "Want to have a picnic sometime?" But the week after a fun day, you want to stay in.
ISFJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and feels settled with set plans. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started inviting people as soon as an idea hits and enjoying the moment. Even after discovering the fun of inviting people, the way you rest hasn't changed. During the picnic, you spend the whole time making sure everyone's having fun, so the next week you need time to stay quietly at home and get your energy back.
ISFJ>ENFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your out-with-friends self or your relaxing-at-home self can give completely different results.
ISFJ>ENFP.plus: You turn down invites because you use a lot of energy when having fun. Once you feel better, you can be the one to invite people again.
ISFJ>ENFP.tip: When you make fun plans, keep the next day empty. When your rest day is already set, you can enjoy yourself fully.
ISFJ>ENFP.hidden: After inviting people, do you double-check the meeting place and time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and even get-togethers you started on a whim can keep going.

ISFJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who follows the rules and helps people in trouble.
ISFJ>ISTJ.body: You properly stick to rules and the usual way of doing things. You take care of monthly bills and paperwork all at once on a set day. At work, if there's a mistake, you say so clearly. But when you see someone in trouble, you can't leave them alone.
ISFJ>ISTJ.body_s: You properly stick to rules and the usual way of doing things. You put things you have to turn in into your bag the night before they're due. In class jobs and clubs, if there's a mistake, you say so clearly. But when you see someone in trouble, you can't leave them alone.
ISFJ>ISTJ.say: "I made the format match last time."
ISFJ>ISTJ.do: You compare each month's electric bill with the same month last year.
ISFJ>ISTJ.do_s: You compare how you spent your allowance each month with the month before.
ISFJ>ISTJ.worry: After pointing something out, you worry you hurt the other person. Some days you can't decide whether to follow the rules or help the person in front of you.
ISFJ>ISTJ.karai: You spot mistakes in other people's paperwork right away, but check your own three times and still feel unsure.
ISFJ>ISTJ.karai_s: You spot mistakes in a friend's report right away, but check your own three times and still feel unsure.
ISFJ>ISTJ.aru: You can properly speak up to someone who missed a deadline. But that night you worry, "Did I say too much?" and the next morning you go check on them.
ISFJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks first about the other person's feelings before acting. As you gained experience, you also came to say what needs to be said clearly, with logic, to keep the rules. Even now that you can call people out, your care for them is the same as ever. Even if you think you were right to say something, you worry about whether the person is feeling down, so the next morning you want to see their face and check.
ISFJ>ISTJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISFJ>ISTJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture homework or class jobs and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISFJ>ISTJ.plus: You worry after pointing things out because you really think about the other person. Everyone trusts someone who's careful and kind.
ISFJ>ISTJ.tip: After pointing something out, add, "You're always a big help." It's easier for them to take, and you won't worry so much at night.
ISFJ>ISTJ.hidden: When someone's feeling down, do you notice right away and talk to them? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even when pointing something out, you can say it in a way that gets through.

ISFJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who gets things ready before anyone's in a bind.
ISFJ>ISFJ.body: You always prepare ahead so the people around you won't run into trouble. You get ready in the same order every morning, and you decide the next day's side dishes for your family's packed lunches the day before. At work, you've often refilled the copy paper before it runs out.
ISFJ>ISFJ.body_s: You always prepare ahead so the people around you won't run into trouble. You get ready in the same order every morning, and you pack what you need the night before. In your club, you've often restocked the athletic tape before it runs out.
ISFJ>ISFJ.say: "Aren't you cold? Want to borrow my jacket?"
ISFJ>ISFJ.do: When someone in your family catches a cold, you have rice porridge and a sports drink ready before they ask.
ISFJ>ISFJ.do_s: When a friend is home sick, you put together notes from that day's classes before they ask.
ISFJ>ISFJ.worry: You find it hard to say no when asked, so your own time can disappear. Doing things for others becomes so normal that some days you lose track of how you feel.
ISFJ>ISFJ.karai: You remember your friends' birthdays, but forget your own until someone mentions it.
ISFJ>ISFJ.aru: "Want me to do that?" is your catchphrase, and before you know it your week is full of favors.
ISFJ>ISFJ.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination, so the way you act first for the people around you has carried on just as it is since way back. When you see someone in trouble, you reach out before you're asked. As long as you have quiet time alone to rest, you can keep going. Helping before someone gets stuck puts you at ease too, so "Want me to do that?" comes out of your mouth before you can say no.
ISFJ>ISFJ.yure: Your temperament and character match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day when favors have piled up and worn you out, your answers may come out a little different.
ISFJ>ISFJ.plus: You can't say no because you picture the other person's troubled face. You act first, and that really helps the people around you.
ISFJ>ISFJ.tip: When someone asks a favor, don't answer right away. Try saying, "Let me check my schedule." A little time makes it easier to say no when it's too much.
ISFJ>ISFJ.hidden: Do you sometimes want to head out without any plan? Going with the moment is something you can do, too. Make a day with no plans now and then, and you'll feel lighter.

ISFJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who loves looking after people and runs things smoothly.
ISFJ>ESTJ.body: You're good at getting lots of things done efficiently and deciding everyone's roles. But you also remember each person's situation. Before an event, you look over last year's job chart and decide ahead of time who to ask for what. At neighborhood events, you might quietly lighten the load for people who can't make it.
ISFJ>ESTJ.body_s: You're good at getting lots of things done efficiently and deciding everyone's roles. But you also remember each person's situation. Before an event, you look over last year's job chart and decide ahead of time who to ask for what. When preparing for the school festival, you might quietly lighten the load for people who can't make it.
ISFJ>ESTJ.say: "If you have little kids, helping in the morning only is totally fine."
ISFJ>ESTJ.say_s: "If you have tutoring, it's totally fine to leave prep early."
ISFJ>ESTJ.do: You gather the family's schedule in a calendar app and send it to everyone every week.
ISFJ>ESTJ.do_s: You gather your club's schedule in a calendar app and send it to everyone every week.
ISFJ>ESTJ.worry: After deciding things quickly, you worry you seemed harsh. When you're in front of people day after day, you want time to relax alone.
ISFJ>ESTJ.karai: You tell everyone, "Go home early," and you're always the one turning off the lights at the end.
ISFJ>ESTJ.aru: You keep the discussion moving and settle the roles fast. But on the way home you worry, "Did I come off as harsh?" and send a message: "Let me know if anything comes up."
ISFJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who spends time quietly alone and decides with the other person's feelings in mind. As the years went by, you also came to stand in front of people and decide things quickly with logic. Even though you decide faster now, your care for others is the same as ever. After a discussion where deciding quickly came first, you worry whether anyone was left behind, and you can't help sending a quick message.
ISFJ>ESTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your in-charge self or your alone-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESTJ.plus: You feel uneasy because you remember each person's situation. Since you decide with even the people who can't come in mind, everyone can take part without strain.
ISFJ>ESTJ.tip: When you assign roles, ask right then, "Tell me if anything's too much." Then you won't need to send a worried message later.
ISFJ>ESTJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved drinking your favorite tea alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Make that time on busy nights, and you'll move smoothly the next day too.

ISFJ>ESFJ.title: At get-togethers, you make sure to talk to each person.
ISFJ>ESFJ.body: At get-togethers, you talk to each person who comes. You remember the restaurant everyone loved before and book it early. You like talking with people, but afterward you want time alone to rest. At New Year's gatherings with relatives, you might even have the envelopes ready for the kids' New Year's money.
ISFJ>ESFJ.body_s: At get-togethers, you talk to each person who comes. You remember the games everyone had a blast with before and get them ready early. You like talking with people, but afterward you want time alone to rest. At New Year's gatherings with relatives, you might even have a card game ready to play with your little cousins.
ISFJ>ESFJ.do: When you run into a neighbor, you remember how their family is doing and ask about them.
ISFJ>ESFJ.worry: After giving it your all at a get-together, you suddenly feel drained and don't want to talk to anyone. Some days you're so busy looking after everyone that you don't enjoy yourself.
ISFJ>ESFJ.karai: You take lots of photos of everyone, but there are hardly any of you.
ISFJ>ESFJ.aru: You agree to organize a reunion and handle both the front desk and the photos on the day. But the next week, you can't bring yourself to reply to friends' invites.
ISFJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by resting alone. As you gained experience, you became able to move around energetically among people too. Still, the energy you use only comes back with time alone, even now. On the day you organize, you use up all your energy among people, so the next week you have no energy left to reply to invitations.
ISFJ>ESFJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your organizer self or your relaxing-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESFJ.plus: You can't reply the next week because you gave it your all on the day. When you talk to each person, people want to come again.
ISFJ>ESFJ.tip: Make the day after a get-together a day you don't have to reply to anyone. If you send a quick "I'll reply tomorrow," you can rest easy.
ISFJ>ESFJ.hidden: Do you feel calm walking alone or listening to your favorite music? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Put that time on your schedule, and you'll keep your energy longer around people.

ISFJ>ISTP.title: For you, quietly helping is easier than talking.
ISFJ>ISTP.body: Rather than encourage people with words, you help them with your hands. When you notice a squeaky door or a flickering light bulb, you fix it before anyone has trouble. When a family member's phone settings are off, you might quietly fix them.
ISFJ>ISTP.say: "It's faster to just try it than read the manual."
ISFJ>ISTP.do: When new furniture arrives, you put it together alone that same day.
ISFJ>ISTP.worry: When someone says "Thank you," you don't know what to say back. When all you can do is listen, you can't help with your hands, and you get restless.
ISFJ>ISTP.karai: You're quick to help with other people's problems, but you never tell anyone about your own.
ISFJ>ISTP.aru: When a friend's umbrella has a bent rib, you fix it and hand it back without a word. When they say "Thanks," you just say, "It's nothing."
ISFJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who values the other person's feelings and prepares properly. Through all kinds of experiences, you got better at figuring things out on the spot and fixing them with your hands. Wanting to help people has been part of you all along, and it shows in your hands more than in your words. Fixing things is a natural way of helping for you, so you don't feel it's worth putting into words.
ISFJ>ISTP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer thinking about fixing something and you lean toward logic and the moment. Think about your family and you lean toward feelings and planning.
ISFJ>ISTP.plus: You get shy because you're not helping to be thanked. Feeling restless just means you really want to be useful to them.
ISFJ>ISTP.tip: When someone thanks you, a smile is enough. When you're just listening, find one thing you can do with your hands, like making them some tea.
ISFJ>ISTP.hidden: Do you prepare gifts ahead of time for the birthdays of people you care about? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, you don't just help in the moment, you can also prepare ahead.

ISFJ>ISFP.title: Someone who suddenly wants to take a detour on the usual route.
ISFJ>ISFP.body: You handle everyday things properly, but you also feel like taking a little detour depending on your mood. Even on the same route every day, you quickly notice newly bloomed flowers or a store's new sign. When the season changes, you might want to switch out the cushion covers in your room.
ISFJ>ISFP.say: "Just the smell of this bakery makes me happy."
ISFJ>ISFP.do: On days off, you buy a single flower you like and put it in your room.
ISFJ>ISFP.worry: Some days you want to follow the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood, and you can't decide. Sometimes, after acting on a whim, you have small regrets.
ISFJ>ISFP.karai: You buy a top you love in several colors, then wear the same one every time.
ISFJ>ISFP.aru: Even on a day that's going to plan, if the weather's nice, you want to take a detour. But afterward, being off-schedule bugs you and you feel a little restless.
ISFJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who feels settled when your day goes as planned. As you gained experience, you also came to enjoy acting on the weather or your mood that day. Even with the urge to take detours, caring about your schedule has been part of you all along. Even while enjoying a detour, you can tell your plans are slowly getting pushed back, so you somehow can't settle down.
ISFJ>ISFP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture work or chores and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISFJ>ISFP.yure_s: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture classes or homework and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISFJ>ISFP.plus: You feel restless after a detour because you really take care of your days. When you talk about a shop you found, it's fun for the people listening too.
ISFJ>ISFP.tip: Put 30 minutes of "detour time" into your plans. Then you can enjoy a detour without it bugging you.
ISFJ>ISFP.hidden: Before a trip, do you naturally decide what to bring and the order you'll go in? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can actually do the things you want to try.

ISFJ>ESTP.title: Someone who jumps in right away when someone needs help.
ISFJ>ESTP.body: When you see someone in trouble, your body moves before you think. If you see someone on the train who looks unwell, you get up from your seat right away and ask if they're okay. If someone drops their things on the street, you go pick them up before anyone else.
ISFJ>ESTP.do: At a sale, when you find something you want, you try it on right there and buy it without hesitating.
ISFJ>ESTP.worry: Some days you wonder afterward whether a quick decision was the right one. Sometimes you help so eagerly that you later think, "Did I overdo it?"
ISFJ>ESTP.karai: You say, "I'm not tired," then you're the first one asleep on the train home.
ISFJ>ESTP.aru: When you help someone move, you start carrying the heavy boxes as soon as you arrive. But back home, you worry, "Did I overstep?"
ISFJ>ESTP.why: Thinking based on past experience is the same in your temperament and your character. The three that differ are how you deal with people, how you decide, and how you go about things. By birth, you're the type who stays calm on your own, thinks about the other person's feelings, and then acts according to plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you also started adjusting to the moment among people and moving your body right away. Even if your body moves first, caring about how the other person felt is still as it was when you were born, so once you're home and calm, you look back and think, "Did I overstep?"
ISFJ>ESTP.yure: Three things differ between your temperament and your character, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself on the move and you'll get an active type. Answer as yourself having a slow talk with someone close and you'll get a quieter type.
ISFJ>ESTP.plus: You think about it afterward because you care how others feel. Someone who moves right away and also cares is someone people count on.
ISFJ>ESTP.tip: When you take something on, first say, "I'll do up to here," then get moving. On nights after a busy day, take some time alone to rest.
ISFJ>ESTP.hidden: By nature, you're good at getting ready ahead of time. Before a trip, don't you quietly check the departure time and what to bring? Share it with everyone, and fewer people will be rushing on the day.

ISFJ>ESFP.title: Someone who notices the person sitting alone in a lively crowd.
ISFJ>ESFP.body: You love lively places and laugh a lot with everyone. When someone is standing off by themselves, you notice right away and talk to them. When taking photos, you call even the people at the edge: "Get in, get in!" At fireworks festivals, you might look for a spot where everyone can see well ahead of time.
ISFJ>ESFP.say: "Isn't it cold over there? I have a lap blanket."
ISFJ>ESFP.do: When you go out, you pack snacks in your bag to share with everyone.
ISFJ>ESFP.worry: After a fun time, you suddenly feel drained and don't want to talk to anyone. After getting excited, you worry about what people thought of you.
ISFJ>ESFP.karai: You laughed and had the most fun, then at home you worry, "Was I too loud?"
ISFJ>ESFP.aru: At parties you get everyone going, but the moment you're in the taxi home, you're so drained you can't say a word.
ISFJ>ESFP.aru_s: At birthday parties you get everyone going, but the moment you're on the train home, you're so drained you can't say a word.
ISFJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges with quiet time alone and acts within a set routine. As the years went by, you also came to ride the fun of the moment among people and get everyone going. Even with that knack for livening things up, the way you recharge is the same as ever. During a get-together, you keep putting out energy so everyone has fun, so the moment you're alone on the way home, all that tiredness hits you at once.
ISFJ>ESFP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your out-with-friends self or your quiet-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESFP.plus: You worry "Was I too loud?" because you think about others' feelings. Because you reach out, fewer people end up alone.
ISFJ>ESFP.tip: After fun plans, decide you don't have to force conversation on the way home. If you say, "I'm a bit tired, so I'll be quiet," everyone will understand.
ISFJ>ESFP.hidden: Before going out, do you settle what to bring and when to head home? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even fun days feel safe.
